summary:
Çorum province stands under the national framework applicable across Türkiye, and that framework presents a structured and documented danger to trans visitors. Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would amend penal-code article 225 to punish conduct "contrary to biological sex" with up to three years in prison, and would allow charges against anyone taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony, carrying up to four years. Under civil-code article 40 the same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 and impose a permanent-infertility mandate, with providers facing fines and up to seven years and patients up to three years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected, and Human Rights Watch called for withdrawal; the measure had not been passed when reported.

Kaos GL's LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025, published 24 February 2026 under the title "A Major Siege", finds that hostility toward LGBT people became explicit state policy during 2025 under "Year of the Family" instructions. The report documents six violations of the right to life, three of them hate-motivated killings, with transgender people the group most affected; 89 torture and ill-treatment violations, up from 51 the previous year; and 313 violations of the right to liberty, roughly two and a half times the previous year and consisting mostly of detentions.

The state maintains no official hate-crime statistics, so Kaos GL's figures rest on media coverage and civil-society monitoring rather than government records. Both the Human Rights Watch analysis and the Kaos GL report are national in scope, and neither records enforcement action, detentions or violent incidents located in Çorum province specifically. A visitor to Çorum should therefore expect the national pattern of documented detentions, hate-motivated violence and pending criminalisation to apply, while recognising that the province itself has no separately sourced record in these materials.
tangentialFactors:
The Kaos GL reporting gap reflects a structural feature of the Turkish legal landscape rather than an absence of incidents in Çorum: because the authorities collect no official hate-crime statistics, provincial-level anti-LGBT violence may occur without entering any citable dataset. Civil-society monitoring that does exist is concentrated in large cities, which biases visible records away from inland provinces.

The draft Judicial Package would, if enacted, convert conduct currently policed through administrative means into offences carrying prison terms, raising the stakes of any encounter with authorities in a province where a visitor's documents and presentation may be compared. The Turkish Medical Association's objection and the refusal of fifteen LGBT groups to accept the draft indicate organised resistance, but neither has prevented the pending provisions from shaping official rhetoric.
localsOnly:
Residents of Çorum face the prospect of criminal penalties for gender non-conforming conduct under a draft that was still pending as of October 2025, alongside an elevated minimum age of 25 for gender-affirming care accompanied by a permanent-infertility requirement that would bind both providers and patients.

Under the Kaos GL national accounting, detentions account for the largest share of recorded liberty violations, and trans people are the group most affected by hate-motivated killings. The absence of state hate-crime record-keeping means local incidents must be self-reported or captured by media monitoring to appear in any dataset.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in this inventory records a specific detention, prosecution, assault or police action in Çorum province. The province-level record is unresolved on the question of whether national enforcement patterns replicate locally, and no Çorum-specific monitoring by Kaos GL or Human Rights Watch has been located here.

Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since the 29 October 2025 report is not sourced in this inventory; its status as pending is carried only up to that date.
